text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- Ministers and deputies from conservative wing of coalition ready to pull out government after a military again draws attention their Islamist partners' role in the rise in fundementalism.
- A draft law presented to the industry ministry aims to lift the state monopoly on sugar prices.
MILLIYET
- Conservative coalition leader Tansu Ciller says she would pull out from the government if Islamists do not hand over the premiership to her before June 18.
- Turkey's leading trade union leader highlights worsening of workers' status in Turkey and rising violation of International Labour Organisation (ILO) standards.
HURRIYET
- A military briefing showed army's belief in the rise of Islamic fundementalism and its determination to fight against it, with arms if seen necessary.
YENI YUZYIL
- Turkish meteorology institute says the abnormally high rainfall in summer is due to pollution carried from Europe.
- Visiting Iranian deputy foreign minister Alaeddin Boroujerdi denies existence of camps of separatist Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) in Iran.
- Shadow remains over dodgy tender for the privatisation of the Erdemir iron and steel factory.
RADIKAL
- Islamist justice minister Sevket Kazan orders investigation against prosecutors and judges who defied his orders to attend a military briefing desscribing alleged rise in Islamist activism.
- The treasury manager of a Turkish bank says the central bank pushes short-term repo rates up to 70 percent to limit foreign currency prices.
DUNYA
- The tender for Akkuyu nuclear power plant is postponed until September 4 to allow three competing consortia to attend.
ZAMAN
- Turkish naval unit in western Izmir province has implemented an army-ordered embargo against doing business with Islamist-owned firms.
CUMHURIYET
- Maritime Trade chamber said five ships were completed in May, at a cost of $100 million.
